subject: gk
question: Lai Haraoba, which literally means ‘the festival of gods’, is primarily celebrated in which state of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Manipur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Lai Haraoba** is a traditional festival celebrated primarily in the northeastern state of **Manipur**.
 
• The term "Lai Haraoba" literally translates to **"the festival of the gods"** in Meitei language, reflecting its religious and cultural significance.
 
• The festival is organized to honor the **deities and ancestors** and is a ritualistic re-enactment of the creation of the universe as per Meitei mythology.
 
• It is celebrated by the **Meitei community**, the largest ethnic group in Manipur, and includes various rituals, dances, and music.
 
• The primary deities worshipped during Lai Haraoba are **Sanamahi, Leimarel Sidabi, and other sylvan deities**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Meitei Mythology:**

 
 
• Meitei mythology is central to the Lai Haraoba festival, which depicts the creation story and the relationship between humans and the divine.
 
• The festival includes the performance of the **"Maibi Jagoi"**, a traditional dance performed by priestesses called Maibis.
 
 
 
• **Cultural Significance:**
 
 
• Lai Haraoba is not just a religious festival but also serves as a platform to preserve and showcase the rich cultural heritage of the Meitei people.
 
• It incorporates elements of music, dance, and oral storytelling passed down through generations.
 
 
 
• **Duration and Celebrations:**
 
 
• The festival usually lasts for several days and involves a series of **rituals, dances, and music performances**.
 
• It is celebrated in various parts of Manipur, particularly in rural areas, where traditional practices are more prevalent.
 
 
 
• **Connection to Nature:**
 
 
• Lai Haraoba emphasizes the connection between humans and nature, with rituals often performed outdoors to honor natural deities.
 
• The festival is also linked to agricultural practices, as it marks the beginning of the sowing season.
 
 
 
• **Other Festivals in Manipur:**
 
 
• Other major festivals of Manipur include **Yaoshang** (similar to Holi), **Ningol Chakouba** (a family-oriented festival), and **Kut** (a harvest festival of the Kuki-Chin-Mizo tribes).
